terms.grammar: ex with the ablative of animus
evidence: Ter. And. 4.4.55; Ter. Ad. 1.1.47 (Lewis & Short), s.v. animus: “from the heart, from the bottom of one’s heart, deeply, truly, sincerely”
Cic. Q. fr. 1.1.5: amāre aliquem ex animō (Lewis & Short), s.v. amō
terms.comment: Opposed to doing a thing for show: Terence, ex animō omnia faciās an dē industriā.

terms.gloss: heart and soul, with one’s whole heart
evidence: Cic. Att. 12.35: cōgitātiōnem tōtō pectore amplectī (Lewis & Short), s.v. amplector

sources: Lewis & Short: animus · Lewis & Short: pectus
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
